domain_restrictions: Lambda ranges over numerical semigroups (cofinite additive submonoids of ℤ_{≥0} containing 0)
genus(Λ)=h means: genus(Λ) is the number of nonnegative integers not in Λ (so this count is finite by cofiniteness)
F(Lambda) is the largest integer not in Λ; if Λ=ℤ_{≥0} then F(Lambda) is defined to be -1
minimal generator x of Λ requires: x ∈ Λ ∩ ℤ_{>0} and (not exists a,b ∈ Λ ∩ ℤ_{>0} such that x=a+b)
effective generator requires: x is a minimal generator and x>F(Λ)
e(Λ) is the cardinality of the set of effective generators of Λ, hence e(Λ) ∈ ℤ_{≥0}
n_h(r) counts genus-h numerical semigroups Λ with e(Λ)=r, so n_h(r) is defined only for r ∈ ℤ_{≥0}
All displayed sums are finite (explicit assumption in the statement)
semantic_sketch_json.normalized_claim: For every h ∈ ℤ_{≥0}, with N(k) the number of numerical semigroups of genus k and n_h(r) = #{Λ : genus(Λ)=h and e(Λ)=r} for r ∈ ℤ_{≥0}, we have the identities (both sums finite): N(h+1) = Σ_{Λ : genus(Λ)=h} e(Λ) = Σ_{r=0}^{∞} r · n_h(r).
quantifier_order: For all r ∈ ℤ_{≥0}, define n_h(r) as a count
Equivalent claim: N(h+1) = Σ_{r∈ℤ_{≥0}} r · n_h(r)

witness_dependencies: For any Λ, the value F(Λ) depends on Λ (largest gap, with special-case value -1 if Λ=ℤ_{≥0})
For any Λ, effective generators are determined by minimal generators x of Λ together with the threshold inequality x>F(Λ)
When asserting that x is a minimal generator of Λ, the decomposition witnesses (a,b) are constrained to lie in Λ ∩ ℤ_{>0} and must satisfy x=a+b; minimality asserts no such witnesses exist
The count e(Λ) depends on the set of effective generators of Λ, hence on both Λ and F(Λ)

statement_nl: Let h be a nonnegative integer. A numerical semigroup is a cofinite additive submonoid of the nonnegative integers containing 0, and its genus is the number of nonnegative integers not belonging to it. For a numerical semigroup Lambda, let F(Lambda) be the largest integer not in Lambda, with the convention F(Lambda) = -1 for the whole set of nonnegative integers. A minimal generator of Lambda is a positive element x of Lambda that cannot be written as a+b with positive a,b in Lambda. An effective generator of Lambda is a minimal generator x satisfying x > F(Lambda). Let e(Lambda) be the number of effective generators of Lambda. Let N(k) be the number of numerical semigroups of genus k. For each integer r >= 0, let n_h(r) be the number of genus-h numerical semigroups Lambda with e(Lambda) = r. Then N(h+1) is equal to the sum, over all genus-h numerical semigroups Lambda, of e(Lambda). Equivalently, N(h+1) is equal to the sum, over all integers r >= 0, of r * n_h(r). All displayed sums are finite.
